articles.title: 53 Years Later, The Greatest Closing Line In Sci-Fi History Is Still The Best Book Quote Of The 1970s
articles.summary: Every once in a while, I come across a line that feels bigger than the book that birthed it. Of course, there are classics with years of literary study behind them that speak volumes on the nature of society, technology, or the world writ large.
body: The world of science fiction literature is home to countless unforgettable closing moments, from 1984 ’s short but devastating retrospective ("He loved Big Brother") to The Three-Body Problem ’s defiant reminder that humanity, like the locust, cannot be so easily wiped out. The best sci-fi endings don't offer comfortable closure, but often reframe everything that came before them. In their closing lines, sci-fi authors love leaving readers suspended in the aftermath, forced to sit with the terrifying mechanics of cold technology, the fragility of human nature, or the vast expanse of space.
points: Every once in a while, I come across a line that feels bigger than the book that birthed it.

articles.title: 15 Years Later, Doctor Who's Darkest Matt Smith Episode Still Has the Greatest Twist
articles.summary: “The God Complex,” which first aired almost exactly 15 years ago, isn’t the scariest TV episode of Doctor Who ever, but it’s up there. It has that unsettling quality many episodes have where the TARDIS crew is suddenly trapped somewhere with no idea how they got there.
body: Toward the end of Matt Smith’s second season in the TARDIS, Doctor Who traps him with Amy Pond (Karen Gillan), Rory Williams (Arthur Darvill), and a small group of random people inside a nightmarish hotel with a huge, muscly minotaur. Each room in the hotel contains a different person’s greatest fear. There are abusive parents, cackling ventriloquist dummies, a scary gorilla, and something the Doctor fears so much that we’re not even allowed to see it.

Amy and Rory don’t leave the show until the following season in the heartbreaking “The Angels Take Manhattan” storyline, but in a very prominent thematic sense, their journey — and Amy’s personal arc in particular — ends with “The God Complex.”
It’s nearly impossible to talk about “The God Complex” without also considering the episode that came right before it, “The Girl Who Waited.”

articles.title: Magic’s Most-Wanted Marvel Deck Is Discounted – Here’s Why You Should Consider This One Instead
articles.summary: Magic: The Gathering’s Marvel Super Heroes set may have given way to the game’s return to Middle-earth with The Hobbit, but that means discounts are getting more regular on the prior, spandex-clad set.
body: The good news is that these savings extend to the Commander Decks, including the Doom Prevails one focused on supervillains from the Marvel Universe. Not long ago, the deck was being sold for significantly more than the MSRP, reaching above $80. Now? It’s dropped from its $75 price to $64.95. And yet, if you’re looking to pick up a deck from the set, it’s not the one I’d recommend.
It pains me to say it in the Year of Doomsday, but Doom Prevails just isn’t the most cohesive deck you can pick up from the set.
It leans into the Connive mechanic to drain foes of life and trigger plenty of discard effects, but it’ll need some elbow grease (and investment) to get it onto the same level as some of its rivals.

There’s a copying subtheme, token generation, and more, but none of it blends together particularly well. That makes the whole deck feel clunky, particularly if this set is your on-ramp to Magic as a whole, or the Commander format.

articles.title: Resident Evil Ending Explained
articles.summary: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil has arrived. But does it have any post-credits scenes, and what does that ending mean for the future of the franchise?
body: You want to know if the new Resident Evil movie has any post-credits scenes or not, right? Well, we’ll tell you right here: There are no scenes after the credits at all.

For years, filmmakers have tried to perfect the Resident Evil formula. Proud wife guy and perpetual video game adaptor Paul W.S. Anderson broke the box office with his six-movie Resident Evil series that evolved into blockbuster action slop (at least by The Final Chapter ). Johannes Roberts stayed faithful to Resident Evil and Resident Evil 2 in his overheated and underperforming reboot, Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City (which received no sequels). Then there’s Andrew Dabb’s Resident Evil show for Netflix, which I didn’t mind all that much, but it never caught on, and Netflix canceled it after a single season.

articles.title: Gundam Rogue Orbit Could Be the Next Great Mech-Action Game
articles.summary: Bandai Namco's new spin on the Gundam franchise is going big on style. Gundam Rogue Orbit is a high-mobility action game that is meant to be a new entry point for players, thanks to a new setting that doesn't require familiarity with five decades of Gundam lore.
body: The initial reveal of Gundam Rogue Orbit drew comparisons to action-focused series like Armored Core, Monster Hunter, and Devil May Cry. After playing the game, those comparisons felt apt in certain ways, but Rogue Orbit does not feel as immediately challenging as, say, 2023's Armored Core 6. Rogue Orbit 's action feels much more melee-focused, with flashy sword, lance, and "whip sword" attacks that hit with the panache of a DMC game.

In short, Gundam Rogue Orbit feels fun, flashy, and often a little button-mashy. The game is not punishing when it comes to combat, nor is it overly restrictive in governing movement and attacks. Yes, your Gundam can temporarily overheat by boosting or shooting too quickly, but rarely did I feel like I was overextending my mobile suit.
points: Bandai Namco's new spin on the Gundam franchise is going big on style.

articles.title: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4, Episode 9 Recap and Review - It's Time for La'An Vs. La'An
articles.summary: With Episode 9, Star Trek: Strange New Worlds proves it's creeping to the finish line of Season 4 like a starship that’s just come out of a battle with a Klingon fleet.
body: Spoilers follow for Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4, Episode 9, “Once La'An a Time.”

Look, I’m sure it’s a lot of fun for the actors on Strange New Worlds to get to drop the Starfleet uniforms for the week and put on exotic dresses and costumes that remind them of their salad days from their college drama programs or whatever, but it’s not as much fun for us to watch. Or, at the very least, it’s not as much fun for me. Not fun at all at this point, in fact.

So yes, “Once La’An a Time” continues Season 4’s trend of doing kooky concept episodes – I’m so sick of typing “concept episode” at this point – but not just that. It’s now doing sequels to concept episodes from previous seasons. In this case, it’s to Season 1’s “The Elysian Kingdom,” where the crew all turned into characters from a storybook, including princesses and wizards and henchmen and warriors and so on. It was a new idea for the show at the time, and it was fun – not to mention that it was also centered on a key emotional storyline for Babs Olusanmokun’s Dr. M’Benga which involved his sick daughter.
points: With Episode 9, Star Trek: Strange New Worlds proves it's creeping to the finish line of Season 4 like a starship that’s just come out of a battle with a Klingon fleet.

articles.title: Lollipop Chainsaw 2 is Officially Bringing Back the Zombie-Slaying Cheerleader Cheesecake Franchise
articles.summary: More than 14 years after the zombie hack-and-slash game Lollipop Chainsaw was released, Juliet the undead slayer returns for an official sequel. While many of the original game's creators — namely DC Studios co-CEO James Gunn and Grasshopper Manufacture's Goichi Suda — don't appear to be involved…
body: Having spent some hands-on time with the build of Lollipop Chainsaw 2: Back2Back that's playable at Tokyo Game Show this week, you should temper your expectations for the long-awaited sequel. It's too early to tell if we really needed another Lollipop Chainsaw.

Lollipop Chainsaw 2: Back2Back is being produced by Nada Holdings and Dragami Games (which was responsible for 2024's remaster, Lollipop Chainsaw Repop ). Also involved is the development company JP Games, which is led by former Square Enix exec and Final Fantasy 15 director Hajime Tabata. Original Lollipop Chainsaw scenario writer Masahiro Yuki and artist Nekoshogun return for the sequel.

According to the official description of Lollipop Chainsaw 2: Back2Back from the PlayStation Store, Juliet will return to the town of San Romero, which has been reborn as "Jaredwood," a metropolis centered around the film industry. "Trapped in a distorted zombie movie world by a mysterious director, Juliet must join forces with her friends to uncover the conspiracy hidden behind the chaos and stop the looming threat of corrupt zombies," the game's description reads.

articles.summary: FX's upcoming anthology TV series Far Cry, based on Ubisoft's hit first-person shooter video game franchise, is adding five more actors to its cast as it heads towards production.
body: Far Cry's showrunners are Noah Hawley (Fargo, Alien: Earth) and Rob Mac (It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia). Previously announced cast members include Mac, Lizzy Caplan, and Steve Buscemi. As an anthology, each new season of Far Cry, which will air on FX and Hulu, will feature a different story, setting, and cast. The show doesn't have a release date as of yet.

On the gaming side, Far Cry has been dormant for a little while now, with the last entry in the game series being 2021's Far Cry 6, which IGN thought was great, giving it an 8 out of 10. Meanwhile, Ubi's recent TV efforts have been good. I reviewed Netflix's animated Splinter Cell Deathwatch and quite liked it.

articles.title: "Publishers are afraid of certain parts of the world": Saber Interactive's message to North American studios is to get their head out of their own geography
articles.summary: Layoffs have been a constant drumbeat in gaming industry news since 2022. Even if the cadence of layoffs seems to have slowed in 2026, the severity of those cuts has not lessened.
body: Cuts like those and the ongoing economic pressures plaguing the industry – rising debt rates, a cost of living crisis, and a memory shortage that is making every aspect of making and playing video games pricier – should have the head of any large studio examining their plans for the future. Especially when games are taking longer to make, costing more to make, and up against a much greater volume of competition than even two years ago.

With all that in mind, when I wasn't talking to Saber Interactive's chief creative officer Tim Willits about generative AI, I wanted to know what he would do if he ran one of those 200-people big-budget game studios. Because say what you like about Saber (and there's a lot of things people like to say about Saber), but the developer is doing well at a time when a lot of other studios and publishers are struggling.

articles.title: Scientists Discovered A New Cat Before Rockstar Could Finish GTA 6
articles.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has been in development since 2015, and a lot of things have happened since then, including the recent discovery a new species of cat. The scientific journal Current Biology disclosed the discovery of Leopardus tilcayo--known as the tilcayo tiger cat--this week.
body: The tilcayo tiger cat is the first new cat species discovered in over 100 years.

Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz, a co-author of the report, told NBC News that it is currently unknown how many of the cats remain in the wild. She said she discovered the cat basically by accident. She volunteers at a wildlife rehab facility close to La Paz, Bolivia and noticed a tiny cat that she thought was a kitten.

The cat was brought to the facility by a man who was caring for it, feeding it rice and eggs, and later giving it up when he was unable to care for it. Genetic testing was undertaken, and it was discovered that it was indeed a brand-new species of cat never before discovered or documented.

As for more gaming-related things that have happened since GTA 5 came out, GameSpot recently assembled a collection of some of the biggest news stories, including Halo coming to PlayStation, the release of 15+ Call of Duty games, the entire run of Phil Spencer as Xbox CEO, and more.

articles.summary: Popcorn buckets for movies are all the rage today. Basically every big movie has one. But they aren't all created equally. One popcorn bucket that looks like it could be the best one yet is for this October's Street Fighter movie.
body: Revealed today by Cody Rhodes, the Street Fighter popcorn bucket, which will be exclusive to AMC locations, is modeled after his character Guile's epic hair. The popcorn goes in the bucket, and then you can put it on your head and grab the popcorn from up there. Or you can plop it in your lap and eat the popcorn normally. In a word, the popcorn bucket is perfect. If you need three words, Rhodes said the popcorn bucket is "aerodynamic, ergonomic, delicious."
Check out the glorious announcement video for the Street Fighter popcorn bucket below.
Tickets for the Street Fighter movie go on sale this coming Monday, September, 21. Presumably that's also when people can reserve one of these popcorn buckets, so the price should be revealed soon.

The Street Fighter movie releases in theaters on October 16. In addition to Rhodes as Guile, the film features Noah Centineo as Ken, Andrew Koji as Ryu, Roman Reigns as Akuma, Jason Momoa as Blanka, 50 Cent as Balrog, David Dastmalchian as M. Bison, and Eric Andre as Don Sauvage.

articles.title: GTA 6 has turned October into a new release bloodbath, but AA first-person soulslike Valor Mortis is hellbent on entering the fray
articles.summary: Judging by the November release schedule, few publishers will dare release within spitting distance of GTA 6. Which is understandable, but it's caused a massive bottleneck in October: Ace Combat 8, Gears of War: E-Day, Star Wars: Galactic Racer and Modern Warfare 4 will all release next month.
body: And that's not including all the other anticipated games not under the wings of a major publisher. I'm talking about a new Hellraiser game, Silver Pines, Jonathan Blow's next one, Planet Zoo 2, a remaster of Tales of Eternia, and the 1.0 launch of Enshrouded. There's even a new Final Fantasy 2D-HD remake.

Joining this fray will be Valor Mortis, a new first-person soulsike ( their words ) by the creators of the Ghostrunner series. It looks better than the concept sounds: a recent demo was well-received, mostly because it seems to nail first-person melee combat, which is famously hard to get right.

I wouldn't dare predict how well or otherwise Valor Mortis will sell when it releases on October 13, but it certainly has its work cut out for it. Its publisher Lyrical Games is well aware of this, as CEO Blake Rochkind told The Game Business in a recent interview.

While probably not the physical disc announcement fans were hoping for, there is enough here for the die-hard collector.
The GTA 6 album will be released in a double-CD set for $20, a double-vinyl set for $50, and a limited edition double-vinyl set for $125.
And finally, Lollipop Chainsaw 2: Back2Back has been announced.
videos.author: IGN

videos.title: Bloodstained: The Scarlet Engagement - Gameplay Trailer | PS5 Games
videos.summary: From the team at ArtPlay and 505 Games comes the latest trailer for Bloodstained: The Scarlet Engagement. Together, heroes Leo and Alex must rise against the Demon Lord Elias in order to free a kingdom from the evil forces that have held it captive.
body: Explore the series’ largest map yet, experience a dynamic day-night cycle, master new abilities with the Epiphany Combat System, and customise each hero with crafting, cooking, equipment and armour.
Bloodstained: The Scarlet Engagement launches on PlayStation 5 in 2027.
